# Testing a package that simd depends on makes the go command compile a test
# variant of it, which a rewritten package (it imports simd) cannot link against.
# The go command compiles packages concurrently, so the variant may not exist yet
# when another package is compiled: the wrapper reads the go command's command line
# and rewrites nothing in a build that tests such a package. testing/iotest has a
# loop the wrapper would rewrite, and the test binary must still link and pass.

env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG=$WORK/log
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_DEBUG=1
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG_PKGS=testing/iotest
exec go test -short -run 'TestSprintf|TestScanf' -toolexec=$LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC fmt
stdout -count=1 '^ok  	fmt	'
cmp log log.want

# Testing a package simd does not depend on is not affected: the same package is
# rewritten again once the tested package is one the wrapper may link against.
env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache2
rm log
exec go test -short -run 'TestReader|TestOneByte' -toolexec=$LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC testing/iotest
stdout -count=1 '^ok  	testing/iotest	'
grep '^rewrote [0-9]+ loop.s. in testing/iotest$' log

-- go.mod --
module example.com/app

go 1.27.1
-- log.want --
skipped testing/iotest: the build tests a package simd depends on
